```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)


## 1. Import White-tailed deer Data

library(readr)

# Import white-tailed deer observations
df_deer <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/NC_WhiteTailedDeer_iNaturalist_public.csv"
)

# Check dimensions
dim(df_deer)

# Check variable names
names(df_deer)

```

## 2. Missing Values Assessment

```{r missing-values}
# Count missing values for each variable
missing_count <- colSums(is.na(df_deer))

# Display missing value counts
missing_count

# Calculate missing percentages
missing_percent <- colMeans(is.na(df_deer)) * 100

# Create a summary table
missing_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(df_deer),
  Missing_Count = missing_count,
  Missing_Percent = round(missing_percent, 2)
)

missing_summary

```
### Interpretation 

This dataset contains 16,595 observations and 37 variables. No missing values for both latitude and longitude. However, 66 observations (0.40%) are missing observation dates. In addition, 3,165 observations (19.07%) are missing positional accuracy information, while 1,938 (11.68%) are missing public positional accuracy information. Several non-essential variables, including sound_url, tag_list, and description, have high proportions of missing values. They are not required for the planned spatial analysis. Overall, the dataset has complete geographic coordinate fields. No observations were removed during this initial assessment.

## 3. Duplicate Observations

```{r duplicate-check}

# Total number of observations
nrow(df_deer)

# Number of unique observation IDs
length(unique(df_deer$id))

# Count duplicate observation IDs
sum(duplicated(df_deer$id))

# Check fully duplicated rows
sum(duplicated(df_deer))
```

### Interperation

This dataset contains 16,595 observations with 16,595 unique observation IDs. No duplicated IDs or fully duplicated rows were identified.

## 4. Observation Quality and Coordinate Obscuration

```{r quality-check}

# Count observations by quality grade
table(df_deer$quality_grade)

# Count observations with obscured coordinates
table(df_deer$coordinates_obscured, useNA = "ifany")

# Calculate percentages of obscured coordinates
prop.table(table(df_deer$coordinates_obscured)) * 100

```

### Interpretation

Among the 16,595 white-tailed deer observations, 15,737 (94.83%) are classified as Research Grade, while 604 (3.64%) are Needs ID and 254 (1.53%) are Casual. Additionally, 2,568 observations (15.47%) have obscured coordinates, 14,027 (84.53%) have unobscured coordinates. Our research focuses on the spatial relationship between deer observations and the wildland-urban interface, obscured coordinates may reduce the accuracy of spatial comparisons.

## 5. Temporal Filtering (2010–2020)

```{r temporal-filter}

# Keep observations from 2010 to 2020
df_deer_filtered <- df_deer[
  !is.na(df_deer$observed_on) &
  df_deer$observed_on >= as.Date("2010-01-01") &
  df_deer$observed_on <= as.Date("2020-12-31"),
]

# Extract observation year
df_deer_filtered$year <- as.integer(
  format(df_deer_filtered$observed_on, "%Y")
)

# Check the number of remaining observations
nrow(df_deer_filtered)

# Check the date range
range(df_deer_filtered$observed_on, na.rm = TRUE)

# Count observations by year
table(df_deer_filtered$year)
```
### Data Quality Summary

The original dataset contains 16,595 white-tailed deer observations. No duplicate observation IDs or fully duplicated rows were identified, and all observations have publicly available geographic coordinates. However, 66 records have missing observation dates, and 2,568 records (15.47%) have obscured coordinates. Positional accuracy information is also incomplete. After restricting the data to 2010–2020, 2,891 observations were retained. Additional cleaning decisions and coordinate validation results are documented in the following sections.


## 6. Select Variables and Export Cleaned Data

```{r select-export}

# Select variables relevant to the analysis
df_deer_clean <- df_deer_filtered[, c(
  "id",
  "observed_on",
  "year",
  "time_observed_at",
  "latitude",
  "longitude",
  "quality_grade",
  "coordinates_obscured"
)]

# Check cleaned dataset dimensions
dim(df_deer_clean)

# Create processed data folder
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Export cleaned dataset
write_csv(
  df_deer_clean,
  "data/processed/NC_Deer_Cleaned_2010_2020.csv"
)

```
